cultural.vision_reason: A hand-woven cap made from strip-woven aso oke cloth in the classic Yoruba indigo, white and black stripe pattern, matching the description of hand-spun indigo cotton with imported white/black thread wefts—an archetypal Yoruba garment.

physical.title: cap; costume
physical.summary: Cap tailored from strips of Yoruba aso oke cloth; the strips are all of the same pattern, and made from hand-spun dyed indigo cotton thread, together with imported European thread of white and black cotton. The strips have been hand-woven and hand-sewn together. The warp is made of stripes of the three colours of thread, while the weft uses an indigo ground together with supplementary float bundles of white and black cotton. In larger pieces of the same cloth (seeAf1991,14.6.b and c.), it can be seen that white cotton has been used in some of the weft to give a further patterning to the fabric. The cap is lined with machine-woven blue cotton.

cultural.vision_reason: This is an indigo tie-dyed (adire) cloth with a spiral "akete" resist pattern, a classic Yoruba textile technique from Nigeria; it matches the claimed ethnicity.

physical.title: adire
physical.summary: Adire cloth: composed of four uneven lengths of machine plain woven European cotton machine sewn together . The textile is decorated using the tie-dyed method. The producer has tied the desired pattern into the textile before dyeing the textile indigo.  The pattern is composed of nine regularly spaced spirals on a background of small circles. This pattern is called AKETE or the 'Caps.'  The hem is machine sewn.

cultural.vision_reason: Classic indigo adire eleko/stitch-resist cloth with concentric circle and stripe motifs, a well-documented Yoruba textile technique made from imported cotton and hand-dyed with indigo resist patterns.

physical.title: adire
physical.summary: Adire cloth: composed of two even lengths of machine plain woven European cotton machine sewn together. The textile is decorated using the stitch-resist and tie-dye method. The producer has sewn the desired pattern into the textile before dyeing the textile indigo. The textile is divided into alternating stripes in the weft direction including narrow stripes which have been stitched into the fabric and spirals which have been created by tying many tiny circles into the fabric prior to dyeing. The textile is bordered by two rows of small circles which have been tied into the fabric prior to dyeing.This pattern is called AKETE 'caps' or 'owner of caps'.  The hem is machine sewn.

physical.title: gown; adire; tobe
physical.summary: Cotton gown (tobe, agbada) made up out of an early adire cloth of machine-made European white calico cloth, tie-died in indigo, creating a white pattern on dark blue, and sewn together to form a gown.
